shopping: This is someone shopping with only a keyboard.
skip: They press Tab to move through the page… and the Add to cart button gets skipped.
scale: That's not rare. In 2026, 95.9 percent of the top million home pages had accessibility failures.
And almost all of them come from the same six mistakes.
title: So we built Curb Cut.
It fixes those barriers from the outside, right in your browser, and proves every fix works.
test: Step one. Kane, an AI testing agent, tries the task the way a disabled person would. It fails.
control: Kane tries again with a mouse. The same task works.
So the website is broken, not the task.
rules: Step two. An agent writes a small, safe fix. Just rules, no code.
prove: Step three. Kane runs the task again with the fix, and it passes. The recording is the proof.
share: Step four. The extension shares the proven fix with everyone who visits that site.
mass-off: Some barriers are whole journeys. On mass.edu, a keyboard user reaches About, and the menu never opens.
mass-on: With Curb Cut, the same keys open the menu, and Enter takes you to the page.
names: For blind users, the most common barrier is a button with no name. A screen reader just says, button.
On Munich Airport, Curb Cut names it: previous slide. Kane found it with the fix, and couldn't without it.
contrast: The most common failure of all is faint text. Curb Cut nudges the colour just enough to be readable, and measures it.
jev: And on pages we've never fixed, there's an experiment. Jev, a fast decision model from TypeSafe, names unlabelled buttons live, in about a second.
On real sites, 13 of its 15 names were right. When it isn't sure, it stays quiet.
results: Then we locked the code and pointed it at 2,050 websites it had never seen.
It fixed 99 of 142 barriers on its own, including 51 of the 89 hard ones.
six: On 400 more new sites, we tested the five other common failures. Curb Cut fixed 76 of 118.
verified: Kane checked random samples of those fixes, and proved 11 of 20, then 7 of 15. Where it couldn't, we say why.
Today, 105 fixes are live in the extension. 61 of them proven by Kane.
owner: And every fix can go back to the site owner: the exact change, with Kane's recording as proof. When the website fixes itself, our patch retires.
close: Curb Cut. Fixing the web for the people it shuts out. Verified by Kane.
teaser-before: On mass.edu, press Tab to About. The menu stays shut.
teaser-after: With Curb Cut, the menu opens. Enter takes you to the page.
